policy: The final human production interface is a masked block in the single Radia Simulink library. Notebook workbenches are retired for every application, including IH. Python and MCP remain the AI interface, executed docs notebooks with parameterized saved WebGUI scenes are the repository example and documentation layer, field-producing Simulink runs emit GMSH .msh v4.1 post-processing artifacts, and the Cubit Export Mesh toolbar remains a Cubit-embedded surface.

library.backend_policy: MEX or ROM may replace a block backend only after numerical parity, error propagation, lifecycle, and long-run stability tests.

spatial_artifact.required_when: the selected mode computes a spatial field

mesh_preflight.timing: after mesh export and before solver initialization
mesh_preflight.required_when: the selected mode consumes one or more .vol meshes
mesh_preflight.material_constants: validated by DesignSpec/configuration, never inferred from labels

applications.title: Electromagnet
applications.optimization_backend: MATLAB-native VIM density adjoint with one state solve and one adjoint solve per gradient evaluation, followed by MMA or SQP. The explicit batch-analysis trigger remains separate.

applications.title: Stream Function
applications.optimization_backend: Explicit Python/headless design or Pareto batch followed by MATLAB-native analytic-gradient MMA/SQP over preassembled stream-function coefficients.

applications.title: Induction Heating
applications.backend_policy: Readable Level-2 MATLAB Eddy and Thermal S-Functions own ports and lifecycle; separate checked radia_mex object handles own native numerical state. Initialization may locate NGSolve runtime DLLs through the configured Python installation, but Python is not a per-step fallback.

applications.title: Magnetic Levitation
applications.backend_policy: A readable Level-2 MATLAB S-Function advances a shared-coordinate, position-dependent HCurl/CLN reduced state and evaluates the exported Lorentz-force operator. Family assembly occurs before simulation and Python is never called per step.
applications.optimization_scope: control optimization only; material topology optimization belongs to radia-em
